title: Apple Update and Device Lifecycle
scenario: IT needs to update all 200 school-issued iPads and 80 MacBooks from iOS 17.3 / macOS 13.6 to iOS 18.2 and macOS 14.7. This is required for a new security policy and app compatibility. The MDM team needs to push these over-the-air updates with zero downtime for students. A teacher refuses the update on her MacBook because she 'cannot risk her students' work disappearing.'
impact: Operational: 280 devices need updates without disrupting teaching. Compliance deadline drives the urgency.
objectives: Plan a phased rollout with a pilot group first
Configure MDM software update policies for iOS and macOS
Execute the pilot and analyze the results
Handle devices that fail the update
Address teacher concerns about data loss during updates
Validate update compliance across the full fleet

evidence.description: MDM software update policy screenshot showing phased rollout config
Pilot group compliance report — typically shows 8 of 20 successful
Full fleet compliance report after rollout completes

decisionPoints.prompt: Twelve devices in the pilot group failed the update. How do you proceed?

options.label: Pull logs from the 12 failed devices, identify the failure pattern, and remediate each device before retrying
options.feedback: Correct. A blanket retry without diagnosis would risk repeating the same failures at scale. Pulling logs and addressing each root cause is the disciplined approach.

options.label: Push them through the same mechanism with a retry and hope they succeed
options.feedback: Pushing the same update again without diagnosis will produce the same failure pattern. This is exactly the kind of approach that creates fleet-wide incidents.

options.label: Exclude the 12 failed devices from the full rollout and revisit them later
options.feedback: Excluding devices without diagnosis leaves compliance gaps. It is better to fix the root cause and then include them in the rollout.

decisionPoints.prompt: One teacher refuses the update on her MacBook because she 'cannot risk her students' work disappearing.' What is the correct response?

options.label: Explain the school's backup policy, provide a documented rollback window, and proceed after she confirms a recent backup
options.feedback: Correct. Acknowledge the concern, ensure the teacher has a verified backup, and explain the institution's update policy. Most refusals resolve with clear information.

options.label: Proceed with the update regardless — compliance with the security policy is non-negotiable
options.feedback: Skipping the conversation creates resentment and may surface legitimate concerns. Take time to address the teacher's worry before proceeding.

options.label: Exclude her device from the update and document her as a permanent exception
options.feedback: Permanent exceptions undermine the security policy and create compliance debt. The update is required; the teacher's data should be backed up before proceeding.

ticket.initialDescription: Fleet-wide update of 200 iPads (iOS 17.3 to 18.2) and 80 MacBooks (macOS 13.6 to 14.7). Zero downtime required. One teacher refusing update.

nodes.title: Plan the rollout
nodes.body: You are about to update 280 devices. Define a pilot group (e.g., 20 devices), a phased rollout plan, the MDM policies to configure, and the success criteria. Open a change ticket and announce the change window.

nodes.title: Configure MDM software update policies
nodes.body: In Jamf Pro, create software update policies: target iOS 18.2 for iPads and macOS 14.7 for MacBooks. Set phased deployment groups. Enable deferral windows per group. Document the policy configuration.

nodes.title: Execute the pilot
nodes.body: Push the update to the 20-device pilot group. Monitor for 24-48 hours. Document the pilot result: 8 of 20 succeeded, 12 failed.

nodes.title: Address the 12 pilot failures
nodes.body: 12 pilot devices failed the update. Determine the correct next step before scaling to the full fleet.

nodes.title: Remediate the failed pilot devices
nodes.body: Pull logs from each of the 12 failed devices. Identify patterns: storage full, supervised state mismatch, OS version too far behind. Apply targeted fixes per device. Re-run the update on the remediated devices.

nodes.title: Handle the teacher refusal
nodes.body: A teacher is refusing the macOS update due to fear of student work loss. Determine the correct response.

nodes.title: Roll out to the full fleet
nodes.body: With the pilot validated and the teacher concern addressed, push the update to the remaining fleet in waves. Monitor for issues. Capture the compliance dashboard in real time.

nodes.title: Validate compliance
nodes.body: Confirm the compliance report shows 280 of 280 devices on the target versions. Spot-check a sample of devices across both groups. Verify the teacher's device updated successfully.

nodes.title: Report to leadership
nodes.body: Write a rollout report for the CIO and principal: total devices updated, duration, issues encountered, teacher communication outcome, and post-rollout notes.
nodes.prompt: Write the leadership update for the OS rollout, including pilot lessons and full-fleet outcomes.

nodes.title: Debrief
nodes.body: Review your score and reflect on phased rollout discipline.

kbOpportunity: Phased OS update rollout on managed Apple devices — always run a pilot group first; pull failure logs before retrying; address end-user concerns with documentation and confirmation of backups rather than blanket exceptions.
